body.statement:
The matrix \(Q^{\mathrm D}\) has orthonormal columns and, viewed as a constant estimator, belongs to \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).  Whenever the target obeys \(\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\le\sqrt{\mu r/n}\), its normalized maximum-row loss satisfies the pathwise inequality
\[
 \mathcal L(Q^{\mathrm D},U)\le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Put \(\vartheta=\pi/(n+1)\).  For integers \(s,t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the product-to-sum identity and the finite geometric-series identity give
\[
 2\sum_{i=1}^n\sin(is\vartheta)\sin(it\vartheta)
 =\sum_{i=1}^n\{\cos(i(s-t)\vartheta)-\cos(i(s+t)\vartheta)\}
 =(n+1)\mathbf 1\{s=t\}.
\]
For clarity, the last equality follows by taking real parts in
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^n e^{ih i\vartheta}
 =\frac{e^{ih\vartheta}-e^{ih(n+1)\vartheta}}
        {1-e^{ih\vartheta}}
\]
for each nonzero integer \(h\) appearing above; the case \(s=t\) then uses
\(\sin^2 x=(1-\cos(2x))/2\).  Every denominator is nonzero because
\(0<|h|<2(n+1)\) in the nonzero cases.  Since \(r\le n\), the displayed orthogonality identity applies to all columns selected in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}hybrid\mbox{-}estimator}\), and hence
\[
 (Q^{\mathrm D})^\top Q^{\mathrm D}=I_r.
\]
Thus \(Q^{\mathrm D}\in\mathbb O_{n,r}\).  It is deterministic, so it is measurable with respect to the observed sigma-field \(\mathcal O_{n,m}\); the definition of \(\mathfrak E_{n,m}\) in \(\mathrm{def:observed\mbox{-}estimators}\) gives \(Q^{\mathrm D}\in\mathfrak E_{n,m}\).

For every row \(i\), \(|\sin(is\vartheta)|\le1\), so
\[
 \lVert e_i^\top Q^{\mathrm D}\rVert_2^2
 =\frac2{n+1}\sum_{s=1}^r\sin^2(is\vartheta)
 \le\frac{2r}{n+1}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \lVert Q^{\mathrm D}\rVert_{2,\infty}
 \le\sqrt{\frac{2r}{n+1}}.
\]
The minimum over \(R\in\mathbb O_r\) in \(\mathrm{def:rowwise\mbox{-}loss}\) is no larger than its value at \(R=I_r\).  The rowwise triangle inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:left\mbox{-}incoherence}\) therefore yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal L(Q^{\mathrm D},U)
 &\le\sqrt{\frac n{\mu r}}
 \left(\lVert Q^{\mathrm D}\rVert_{2,\infty}
       +\lVert U\rVert_{2,\infty}\right)\\
 &\le\sqrt{\frac{2n}{\mu(n+1)}}+1
 \le1+\sqrt{\frac2\mu}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This is deterministic and hence holds on every sample path.
